description:
FILED s446k (Opus, agent K of round 5), found probing #463 item 5.

  $^R = 7; print "e=[$^R]\n";
    perl: e=[7]
    PCL:  e=[]

Every other caret variable spelling PCL supports round-trips; `$^R` (the
result of the last successful `(?{ })` code block) does not.  Two possible
causes and the discriminating measurement is cheap: transpile the two lines
and look at whether the ASSIGNMENT emits a store at all, or whether it stores
into a cell the READ does not consult (the #412 caret-name machinery spells a
caret variable with a pipe-quoted CL symbol; a mismatch between the two
spellings would produce exactly this).

Blocks the `*^R = *g` half of task #562: aliasing a glob to a variable that
does not work buys nothing.

Low priority on its own (`$^R` is only meaningful with `(?{ })` regex code
blocks), but it is one row in t/re/pat.t and it is a two-minute probe.


DONE s448o (Opus, agent O of round 6), commit 97f1ced (rebased).

THE DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT THE TASK NAMED CAME BACK NEGATIVE, and that is
the finding: the assignment and the read BOTH emit `|$^R|`.  `./pl2cl` on the
two-line repro gives `(p-setf |$^R| 7)` and `|$^R|` -- one spelling, no
mismatch.  So it was not the #412 caret-name machinery.

CAUSE: `(defvar |$^R| nil)` -- a RAW value, not a p-box.  `box-set` returns
silently when its place is not a p-box (documented, by design: it is how a
write to *p-undef* is a no-op), so the store vanished and the read answered
undef.  A magic scalar a program may ASSIGN to has to be a box, like
$^P/$^D/$^F/$^I/$^M.

FIX: the defvar moves ~700 lines down, beside those siblings, as
`(make-p-box *p-undef*)`.  It HAD to move: `make-p-box` is defined ~200 lines
below where $^R used to sit, so the initializer could not be written in place.
Initial value *p-undef*, which is what perl reads before the first (?{...})
block; PCL never runs one, so nothing else ever sets it.

PROBED vs perl 5.40.3, identical in both: undef-before-write, defined(),
numeric context, string assignment, \$^R writing through.  Guard
Pl/t/caret-vars-01.t rows 1-2, inverse-run against the old raw defvar (both
fail there).

FILED FROM THE SAME PROBES: #600 (`local $^P = 5` is a silent no-op -- the
local let binds the BARE symbol while every read emits the pipe-quoted one) and
#602 (`*A = *B` does not clear the slots B lacks).
subject: `$^R` is inert: assignment and read both produce nothing (`$^R = 7; print $^R` prints empty where perl prints 7)
